newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France orders 10 Airbus, 10 Boeings.
newsitem.headline: Air France orders 10 Airbus, 10 Boeings.

text.p: State-owned Air France said on Wednesday its board has approved orders for 10 Airbus A340-300E planes and placed options for five more, and orders for 10 Boeing B777-200 IGW jets, with options for a further 10.

The five Airbus options can be converted to the planned A340-600 model, which would make Air France a launch customer for the "stretched" version of the long-haul, wide-body plane, the airline said in a statement.
The Airbus order consists of five new A340s equipped with CFM56-5C4 engines, in addition to five A340s that it ordered in June 1996, due for delivery between autumn 1997 and the end of 1998, it said.
The A340-200E is the 271-tonne version of the four-engine plane. It will seat 252 in a three-class layout.

The Boeing order replaces a previous order for 15 Boeing aircraft and consists of the heavier "Increased Gross Weight" version of the basic 777-200, equipped with GE90 engines built by General Electric and France's Snecma.
The earlier order, which has now been cancelled, consisted of seven B767-300 and eight B737-500 which had been due for delivery by March 2001, the airline said.
The B777-200 will seat 288 passengers in three-classes and is particularly suited for business class travel.
Due to financial problems, the airline froze at the end of 1994 all its orders, including the Boeing order which dated back to 1989, and opened talks with the two plane makers, it said.
Since then, Air France has restructured its network and optimised fleet use. It has over the past two years increased the number of flying hours by 14 percent.
